artworks.title: Title Page to John Boys' Works
artworks.description: This is a detailed frontispiece of a literary work by John Boys. It includes heraldic shields, architectural elements, and textual inscriptions. In the central oval, the dedication to "The Workes of John Boys, Doctor in Divinity" is featured, surrounded by decorative scrollwork. On the left, an interior scene shows a figure seated at a desk, writing, with the Latin inscription “Scriba doctus in regno celorum.” Opposite, another figure in a library setting gestures thoughtfully, annotated by the phrase "Confitare Mei." Above, an allegorical scene depicts a kneeling figure between two large hands emerging from clouds. The bottom area shows a man at a lectern, framed by elegant motifs.

artworks.title: William Cecill, First Baron Burghley
artworks.description: The image is a portrait engraving of a man. He is depicted from the chest up, facing slightly to his right. The man has a neutral expression, with detailed facial features including eyes, a beard, and a mustache. He wears a hat with a jewel, a ruffled collar, and a patterned robe with decorative elements. His right hand holds a staff. The background is textured, and an arch surrounds the image with text. Below the portrait, there is delicate lettering listing titles associated with Sir William Cecil, Knight.

artworks.title: Edward, the Black Prince at the Age of 49
artworks.description: The image shows a man wearing ornate armor, standing confidently with a spear in one hand and a shield nearby. He has long hair and a beard, with intricate armor pieces such as a breastplate, gauntlets, and greaves. The background contains text describing his identity and achievements.

artworks.title: Edward VI
artworks.description: The image shows a young person facing slightly to the right. They have a gentle expression, round facial features, short hair, and are wearing a crown adorned with jewels, holding a scepter. Their attire includes embellished robes, a large collar, and a cross pendant. The background is plain with a decorative border framing the subject.

artworks.title: Gustavus Adolphus
artworks.description: The image shows a man from the waist up sitting in a formal posture. He has a mustache and goatee, styled hair, and wears ornate attire with a lace collar and shoulder piece. He holds a baton or staff in his right hand. The portrait is in an oval frame with cherubs and decorative elements. Above the frame is a cartouche with scrollwork and cherubs holding a laurel wreath. The background has intricate patterns.

artworks.title: Gustavus Adolphus
artworks.description: The image is an engraving of Gustavus Adolphus from the upper half of his body. His posture is formal, with his body slightly turned and his face towards the viewer. He has short hair, a beard, and a mustache. He wears elaborate clothing with a high collar and armor, holding a baton. The frame around him is decorated with intricate patterns, cherubs, banners with text, and various weapons below. The background has detailed designs and inscriptions.

artworks.title: Henry VIII
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man from the waist up, facing forward. He has a round face, closely set eyes, and a trimmed beard. His hair is styled in a historical manner, partly covered by an elaborate crown. He wears a detailed garment with a decorative collar, fur-trimmed cloak, and intricate patterns. He dons robes indicating wealth and status, with a chain of office across his chest. He holds a scepter and an orb, symbols of authority and royalty. The background is a plain surface. The inscription "Regem dedi iratus eis" is below the portrait.

artworks.title: John Talbot, First Earl of Shrewsbury
artworks.description: The image depicts a historical figure from the waist up. The individual faces slightly to the right, holding a sword in their right hand with the blade pointing upwards. The individual has a pronounced nose, full lips, and a determined expression. The figure wears a helmet with a plume, intricate armor with detailed engravings, and shoulder plates with ornate patterns. They also wear a chain with a medallion around their neck. The background features an oval frame with a coat of arms at the top and a lion emblem on the left, within decorative panels. The bottom section likely contains an inscription about the historical figure on a document or plaque.

artworks.title: John Talbot, First Earl of Shrewsbury
artworks.description: The image shows the upper half of a person depicted in a portrait, who is facing slightly to the right while holding a sword with their right hand. The person has a rounded face with prominent cheeks, a small mouth, and eyes gazing forward. They have short hair beneath a helmet adorned with a decorative bird. The individual is wearing an elaborately detailed suit of armor with ornate designs, including shoulder guards and a richly patterned breastplate, featuring a medallion hanging around their neck. Surrounding them are various heraldic motifs and designs, including two coats of arms in the top corners. The background consists primarily of curved lines that frame the figure, while below, there is text describing their noble titles and achievements.

artworks.title: Title Page for Sylva Sylvarum, Francis Bacon
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a globe suspended between two pillars with ornamental details, with the heavens above. Two winged cherubic heads are depicted above, surrounded by clouds and rays of light emanating from a central point where Hebrew text is placed. The lower half of the image features the drawing of a large globe labeled "Mundus Intellectualis" resting on a scroll, which bears the text "SYLVA SYLVARUM or A NATURAL HISTORY." The surrounding scene is embellished with clouds and celestial elements. A banner near the bottom contains information about the work's authorship and publication, dated 1629. The composition blends elements of classical architecture and celestial representation, with detailed etching that emphasizes texture and contrast.

artworks.title: Title Page for Holy Oyle for the Lampes of the Sanctuarie, John Clarke
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring religious iconography and text. The drawing depicts a detailed composition of various figures and scriptural references. At the top of the image, there is a central figure seated under a cloud, surrounded by an audience of people. Surrounding this central scene are panels with figures labeled as "K. Solomon," "Isaiah," "St. Paul," and "Apollos," each holding scrolls or books and accompanied by scriptural or philosophical quotations. The lower part of the image contains the text "HOLY OYLE FOR THE LAMPES OF THE SANCTUARIE. Or Scripture Phrases Alphabetically disposed." The composition includes ornate scriptural elements such as candlesticks and celestial symbols, presented with an architectural framing.

artworks.title: Title Page to Sir William Cornwally's Essays
artworks.description: Two individuals are seated under separate archways. They are visible from the head down to their feet, engaged in activities at small tables. The person on the left is reading a book, and the person on the right is writing with a quill pen. Each wears a broad-brimmed hat that partially obscures their facial features. Their clothing is typical of the period, with long coats and high collars. On the tables in front of them are inkpots. The background features detailed arches and columns, and a fabric sign above their heads displays text related to the work depicted in the image.

artworks.title: Title Page to Sir William Cornwally's Essays
artworks.description: The image shows two individuals sitting at separate tables, writing with quills on sheets of paper. Both have similar features and wear clothing typical of early 17th-century fashion. The setting includes arches and columns framing each individual. Each table has an inkpot and a candleholder with an extinguished candle. Above them is a decorative element with the title "ESSAYES" and other details. The background is a plain surface.

artworks.title: Title Page to John Weever, Ancient Funeral Monuments
artworks.description: This is an image of an ornate title page from an old book. The central part shows an intricate, framed frontispiece with the title "Ancient Funerall Monuments within the United Monarchie of Great Britaine, Ireland, and the Ilands adjacent." The frame features classic columns, a pediment with sculptural busts and finials. On the left side is a skeletal figure, possibly representing death, and on the right, a draped human figure representing life or resurrection. Below the text block is an illustrated vignette of a church and cemetery, with the phrase "Hic jacet" (Here lies) written in Latin. Latin inscriptions surround the visual elements, adding to the scholarly atmosphere of the book.

artworks.title: Title Page to An Apologie, or Declaration of the Power and Providence of God
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate title page. The image features an elaborate and symbolic design centered around the title of a publication, “An Apologie or Declaration of the Power and Providence of God in the Goverment [sic] of the World” by George Hakewill. The title is set within a large architectural structure consisting of columns and an arch. Above the arch, a scene depicts a city with figures of a bearded old man holding a scythe and a skeleton. There are also symbols of religious significance, including the Hebrew name of God (YHWH), angels, and apocalyptic imagery. Below, there are emblematic images like a ship on tumultuous seas and a coat of arms with a heart and wings. The composition conveys themes of mortality, divine providence, and the celestial cycle.

artworks.title: Title Page to Ovid's Metamorphosis, translated by G. Sandy
artworks.description: This is a detailed title page for "Ovid's Metamorphosis." The image includes various figures and symbolic elements arranged around the central text "Ovid's Metamorphosis Englished by G. S. Imprinted at London MDCXXVI Cum Privilegio." In the central area, two female figures in classical attire stand on either side of the text. Various figures with attributes are depicted beneath them, including a lyre and symbols of authority. A dynamic depiction of a charioteer riding through clouds is shown above with the text "AD AETHERA VIRTUS." Below the central text are symbolic representations labeled "AMORE" and "SAPIENTIA." The drawing features intricate engravings, classical motifs, and ornate borders.

artworks.title: Achmet I, Sultan of Turkey
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait of a man facing forward. He wears an Ottoman-style tall hat with a crescent motif and an ornate robe with fur trim. The portrait is surrounded by an ornate oval frame with decorative elements and an inscription that includes the name "ACOMATH" and Ottoman family titles.

artworks.title: Lancelot Andrewes, Bishop of Winchester
artworks.description: The image shows the upper body of a man facing slightly to his left, looking towards a book he is holding. He has pronounced facial features, a high forehead, defined eyebrows, and a connected mustache and beard. He wears a flat cap, formal clothing, and holds an open book in his left hand while pointing to a page with his right hand. There is a decorative oval frame in the background with a fine cross-hatching pattern, an inscription below the portrait identifying him as "The right reverend Father in God Lancelot, Bishop of Winchester, and Prælate of the Garter," and a coat of arms.

artworks.title: John Carter
artworks.description: The engraving depicts a man seated at a table with his head turned slightly to the left and tilted upwards. He has a pointed nose, thin lips, a beard, mustache, high forehead, receding hair, and neatly combed back hair. The man wears a dark, formal garment with a ruff collar. On the table in front of him are an inkpot with a quill, an open book, and an hourglass. The background has a dark, patterned texture, and there is Latin text at the top and bottom of the image.

artworks.title: Sir George Croke
artworks.description: The image shows an engraved portrait of a man's upper body. He is positioned at a slight angle, facing slightly to the left, with his hands visible, one of which appears to be holding a cylindrical object resembling a scroll. His facial features include prominent cheekbones, a faintly furrowed brow, and a serious expression. He has thin, wispy hair, slicked back, and a short, full beard with a thread of white. The man is wearing a fur-trimmed robe with a large, ornate ruff around his neck. Surrounding the oval-framed portrait is a decorative pattern of ribbons and banners showcasing Latin text. Below the portrait is a crest set on top of books. The background features intricate line patterns, focusing attention on the detailed depiction of the man’s face and attire.

artworks.title: George Clifford, Third Earl of Cumberland
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man from the waist up. He is facing forward with his head turned slightly to the right. The man has long, slightly wavy hair that falls on his shoulders and a styled goatee. His facial features include sharp eyebrows, deep-set eyes, a straight nose, and thin lips. He is dressed in ornate armor with intricate patterns and a detailed collar, a patterned sash over his shoulder, holding a staff in his right hand. He wears a medallion around his neck. The background has a decorative border with scrolls and inscriptions, two figures with swords, a coat of arms with Latin inscriptions, and an angel-like figure at the bottom.

artworks.title: George Clifford, Earl of Cumberland
artworks.description: The image depicts an engraved portrait of a man shown from the mid-torso upwards, positioned facing the viewer with his head slightly turned to his right. He has a long, pointed beard, a mustache, and wavy, shoulder-length hair. He wears ornate period clothing, a ruffled lace collar, a patterned garment, a sash, and holds a long staff or baton in his right hand. He wears a large chain around his neck with a decorative pendant. The portrait is surrounded by an ornate frame with heraldic symbols, banners, and two figures on each side. In the background above the frame are decorative motifs, including a coat of arms, and below the portrait is an inscription about the person depicted.

artworks.title: Sir Francis Drake
artworks.description: This image is a portrait of a man displayed from the waist up. He is seated in a slightly turned position, with his face turned towards the viewer. The man has short, curly hair that is slightly lighter in color and a pointed moustache and beard. He is dressed in a richly detailed garment, which includes a high collar with intricate patterns and a draped sash. One hand is resting on a globe, and he is holding a nautical staff. Behind him, there is a coat of arms. Below the portrait, there is an inscription composed of several lines of text. The background features wavy horizontal lines, and navigational tools such as an armillary sphere are visible on a table beside him.

artworks.title: Sir Francis Drake
artworks.description: This image depicts a man in a half-length portrait, facing slightly to the right with his head turned towards the viewer. He has distinct facial features, including a neatly trimmed mustache and beard, curly styled hair pushed back, and a receding hairline. The man is wearing a historical garment with intricate layering, a ruffled collar, and cuffs. He has a cloth over one shoulder, holding a staff or rolled paper in one hand and resting his fingers on a globe in the other hand. To his right, there are navigational tools such as a compass bowl and a small globe. Above him, a coat of arms displays two Latin phrases: "CXVXILIO. DIVINO" and "SIC PARVIS. MAGNA." The background features detailed linear patterns, emphasizing the subject and associated symbols.
